questions.q: What real problem does copy-pasting the same loop into three different scripts create?
options: Each copy automatically updates itself when one is fixed
Loops can only legally appear once per machine
A bug or a changed tag name has to be fixed in every copy by hand, with a real risk of missing one
PowerShell refuses to run a script containing a copy-pasted loop
questions.explain: Duplicated logic has to be maintained in every location it was copied to, and it's easy to miss a copy when fixing a bug or updating a value like a tag name.

questions.q: In a function's param() block, what does [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)] do?
options: Has no real effect in PowerShell functions
Requires that parameter to be supplied, rather than letting the function run silently without it
Deletes the parameter if it is left out
Makes the parameter accept only numeric values
questions.explain: Mandatory parameters cause PowerShell to prompt for or error on a missing value instead of silently proceeding without it.

questions.q: Once Get-StoppedVMs is defined, how is it called?
options: It can only be run by pasting its entire body into the console every time
It requires a separate GUI tool to invoke
It can only be called from inside Azure Automation, never from a local session
The same way a built-in cmdlet is called, e.g. Get-StoppedVMs -ResourceGroupName "rg-prod-web"
questions.explain: A custom function named with the Verb-Noun pattern is called exactly like any Az cmdlet, by name and parameter.

questions.q: In the lesson's example, what does Start-AllStoppedVMs do with Get-StoppedVMs?
options: Deletes Get-StoppedVMs after running once
Has no relationship to Get-StoppedVMs at all
Redefines Get-StoppedVMs with entirely different logic
Calls it and loops over whatever it returns, instead of repeating its filtering logic
questions.explain: Start-AllStoppedVMs calls Get-StoppedVMs and pipes its output into ForEach-Object, reusing the filtering logic rather than duplicating it.

questions.q: Why does wrapping logic in a function also make it easier to test?
options: Functions cannot be tested at all, only entire scripts can
Functions automatically generate their own test suites
A function can be called on its own, with specific input, and its output checked independently of the rest of a script
Testing is only possible for code inside a function, never for any other PowerShell code
questions.explain: A single, named function with one clear job can be exercised in isolation, which is exactly what tools like Pester build on later.
